questions.question: What is poverty gap?

options.text: the difference between poverty line and actual income level of all those living below that line
gap between developed and developing nations
gap between the rich and the poor
gap between infrastructural facilities in developed and developing nations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option** __1__**, i.e. __**the difference between the poverty line and actual income level of all those living below that line**__

 
• The **poverty gap **calculates the **intensity of poverty**. It reflects the extent to which people on **average fall under the poverty line**.
 
• The theory of poverty gap was created by** the World Bank** and is largely used to estimate the **incidence of poverty **in different nations worldwide.
 
• The **higher poverty gap reflects a lower level of deprivation** and a **higher incidence of poverty** for those who are below the poverty line. In effect, the government has to provide more income to take them above the poverty line.

questions.question: Which Five Year Plan adopted Indicative Planning in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e __**Eighth**__

__**Eighth Five Year Plan (1992 - 1997)**__ adopted **Indicative Planning** in India.

 
• A form of economic planning, Indicative planning is implemented by a state to solve the issue of imperfect information in the market and mixed economies.
 
• This is done to **increase economic performance**.
 
• Indicative Planning was first attempted in **France.**
 
• India’s Eighth Five Year Plan men­tions that planning would have to be reoriented so as to make it indicative.

questions.question: In Indian Parliament, under which condition a house can declare the seat of a member vacant?

options.text: If member is absent from all meetings of the house for 60 days continuously
If member is absent from all meetings of the house for 45 days continuously
If member is absent from all meetings of the house for 30 days continuously
If member is absent from all meetings of the house for 21 days continuously

questions.solution:
• If member is absent from all meetings of the house for 60 days continuously, a house can declare the seat of a member vacant.
 
• Article 101 of the Constitution of India deals with disqualification of members. It lays down several ways in which the seat may become vacant.
 
• Article 101 (4) provides that the House may declare the seat vacant if the member is absent for a period of sixty days, not counting any period when the House is prorogued or adjourned for four or more consecutive days.

Other cases by the seat of a member can be vacated are:

 
• If the court declares his Election as void.
 
• If the house expels him.
 
• If he becomes the President or Vice - President of the nation.
 
• If he becomes the Governor of a state.

questions.question: There are usually three Parliamentary sessions in India, viz, the Budget session, the Monsoon session, and _______.
questions.solution:
There are usually three Parliamentary sessions in India, viz, the Budget session, the Monsoon session,and the Winter session.

The period during which the Houses - Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha - meet to conduct its business, is called session.

There are three types of Sessions that are conducted in the Parliament of India:

 
• Budget session: from February to May.
 
• Monsoon session: from July to September.
 
• Winter session: from November to December.

The Constitution empowers the president to summon each House at such intervals that there should not be more than a six-month gap between the two sessions.

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are the function(s) of bile juice released from the liver?

I. Make the food coming from stomach alkaline.

II. Conversion of proteins into amino acids.

III. Break down of fats into smaller globules.
questions.solution:
Bile makes the food coming from the stomach alkaline.

Break down fats into smaller globules.

__**EXPLANATION:**__

 
• The liver secretes bile. When bile leaves the liver, it gets stored in the gallbladder, before being released into the duodenum.
 
• When it gets released from the gallbladder, it breaks large fat globules into smaller particles. This is known as emulsification.
 
• As Bile is alkaline in nature, it neutralizes acidic food coming from the stomach to provide the alkaline conditions needed in the small intestine.

questions.question: The wing of a bat and the wing of a bird are the examples of ______ limbs.
questions.solution:
The wing of a bat and the wing of a bird are the examples of Analogous limbs.

Organs having different structure and components but perform similar functions are called Analogous organs.

questions.question: As per the announcement by the government in August 2017, Banks importing gold and precious metals will have to pay ______ tax under the GST.
questions.solution:
As per the announcement by the government in August 2017, Banks importing gold and precious metals will have to pay 3% tax under the GST.

• GST stands for Goods and Services Tax. It is an indirect tax which is levied in India on the supply of goods and services. It was launched at midnight on 1 July 2017 by the former President of India, Pranab Mukherjee, and the Government of India.

questions.question: On 3 January 2018, Lok Sabha passed Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (Amendment) Bill, 2017. The Bill empowers ______ to allow works in a prohibited area.
questions.solution:
On 3 January 2018, Lok Sabha passed Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (Amendment) Bill, 2017. The Bill empowers Central Government to allow works in a prohibited area.

 
• The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (Amendment) Bill, 2017 amends the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958.
 
• AMASR Act, 1958 prohibits construction in the ‘prohibited areas’ even if it is for public purposes. The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (Amendment) Bill, 2017 amends this provision and permits construction of public works in these particular areas for public purposes.

questions.question: Find the work done (in J) when a charge of 20 C moves across a potential difference of 4 V.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 80__ J__.

**__CALCULATION:__**

Given that:

Charge = 20 C

Potential Difference = 4 V

work done = charge x potential diff

 = __4 × 20__

 = 80 J

__The work done in passing a charge of 20 C between two points having a potential difference of 4 V will be 80 J__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__

Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage or potential difference across the two points.

 
• V = I R
 
• R ={ Vover I}
 
 
• V = Voltage
 
• I = Current
 
• R = Resistance or a constant

questions.question: The magnitude of the gravitational force will be equal to the _______.

options.text: product of mass and acceleration due to the gravitational force.
ratio of mass and acceleration due to the gravitational force.
ratio of acceleration due to the gravitational force and mass.
reciprocal of product of mass and acceleration due to the gravitational force.

questions.solution:
The magnitude of the gravitational force will be equal to the product of mass and acceleration due to the gravitational force.

 
• The Universal Law of Gravitation says that – any two objects having mass will attract each other with a force which is directly proportional to the product of their masses.
 
• This force is also inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• Let us understand from the derivation,

According to the Universal law of Gravitation,

F = Gfrac{{{{m}} times {{M}}}}{{{{{r}}²}}}--------Equation (1)

Here, m is the mass of the object,

and Mis the masses of the Earth, which is 6 × 10²⁴ kg

r is the radius of the Earth, which is 6.4 × 10⁶m

F is the gravitational force acting between them, and

G is the gravitational constant, which is 6.7 × 10⁻¹¹ Nm²/kg².

 
• We know that F = ma, where ‘a’ is the acceleration of the body.----------Equation (2)
 
• Equate both the equations,

ma = Gfrac{{{{m}} times {{M}}}}{{{{{r}}²}}}

​a = Gfrac {{M}}{{{{{r}}²}}}--------Equation (3)

a = frac{{6.7 times {{10} ⁻ ¹¹} times 6 times {{10}²⁴ }}}{{6.4 times {{10}⁶}}}

a = 9.8 ms⁻²

**The acceleration ‘a’ here is nothing but the acceleration due to gravity i.e. g, which is 9.8 ms⁻²**

Hence F = ma, can also be written as

F= mg

questions.question: The power of ________ is expressed in terms of a magnitude on a scale called Richter scale.
questions.solution:
The power of an earthquake is expressed in terms of a magnitude on a scale called the Richter scale.

 
• Richter scale was developed by Charles F. Richter in 1935.
 
• The magnitude of the earthquake is found by using the logarithm of the amplitude of the largest seismic wave.
 
• The logarithmic scale runs from 1 to 9, though no upper limit exists.
 
• The earthquake of magnitude 7 is 10 times more powerful than the earthquake of magnitude 6.

questions.question: The _______ has emerged as a convenient means of global communication, information sharing and services.
questions.solution:
The Internet has emerged as a convenient means of global communication, information sharing and services.

 
• A huge network of millions of computer networks constitutes the Internet. These networks are connected by telephones, underwater cables, and satellites.
 
• A computer network, also known as a data network, is a telecommunications network which allows computers to exchange its data.
